After years of Christmas gifts she never wore, this one changed everything.
Every Christmas, same story. I'd spend hours trying to find something she'd actually like. Something meaningful.
Years of trying. Different gifts every time. 
Always that same polite "thanks mom."
I don't think she ever wore any of them.
Then I saw these pearl cross necklaces on Instagram. And honestly, what caught me wasn't the necklace itself.
It was a comment I read.
"I got matching ones for me and my daughter. We both wear them every day."
And something just clicked.
What if we matched?
What if instead of giving her something and hoping she'd like it, we BOTH wore the same thing?
Because here's the thing.
Every gift I'd ever given her was one-way. Here's something FOR YOU.
But if we matched? It's not a gift. It's something we share.
There's no pressure on her because I'm wearing it too.
That felt different.
I checked the reviews, women wearing theirs over a year, still perfect. And they have a lifetime warranty. If it ever tarnishes, they replace it for free.
So I ordered them right away.
Viole Grace was running buy one get one free for Christmas. One for me, one for her. 
When they arrived, the pearls with the gold looked even better in person.
I put mine on right away and wore it every day for two weeks before Christmas.
I wanted to test it before I gave her hers.
Showered in it, worked out in it, slept in it.
Still looked brand new.
Christmas morning, I gave her the box. But I was also wearing mine.
She opened it. Looked at the necklace. 
Then she looked up at me.
And saw I was wearing the exact same one.
"Wait, we match mom?"
"We do," I said.
She put it on right there over her pajamas and hugged me.
That was four months ago.
She wears it every single day.
And honestly, I don't know if it's the cross, or the fact that it actually doesn't tarnish and is waterproof so she can wear it 24/7, or just the matching thing.

criativos.title: Lifetime Color Warranty✨
criativos.bodyText:
A stranger on a plane saw me holding my cross at 30,000 feet and said four words that broke me open in the middle of the night.
11:45 PM. Gate B7. The flight to Charlotte is already boarding and I'm the last one in line.
I hate flying at night. I hate flying alone even more. But dad had another fall and mom can't do this by herself anymore, so here I am, boarding a red-eye with a carry-on and a knot in my stomach that won't go away.
I found my seat. Middle row. The woman by the window is already asleep. I buckle in, put my bag under the seat, and my hand goes right where it always goes.
My cross.
I've been doing that for months now. Every time the anxiety hits, every time the phone rings and my heart drops, my fingers find this little pearl cross and I just hold it. I don't even think about it anymore. It's just what my body does when it needs something solid.
The cabin lights go off. I can't sleep.
I'm sitting there in the dark holding my necklace, running the pearls between my fingers, praying the same prayer I've been praying since September.
Just let him be okay. Just one more good day.
Around 2 AM the woman in the aisle seat turns to me. I didn't even realize she was awake.
She looks at my hand on my chest and says quietly,
"My daughter has the same one."
I don't know what to say so I just nod.
"She wore hers through my husband's chemo. Never took it off. Not once."
"She said it was the only thing that made her feel like God was still in the room."
And I just lost it. Right there in seat 14C in the dark at 30,000 feet with a stranger who somehow knew exactly what I was going through without me saying a single word.
We talked for the rest of the flight. She told me about her husband, I told her about my dad. She showed me a photo of her daughter. We cried. We laughed. We prayed together right there in the middle row of a plane full of sleeping strangers.
When we landed she hugged me at the gate and said,
"That necklace found you for a reason."
That was six weeks ago.
I've worn it every single day since. Showers. Hospital visits. Late night drives to my parents' house. It still looks exactly the same as the day I put it on. Not a single tarnish mark. Not one sign of wear.
It comes with a lifetime color warranty. If it ever loses its color they replace it. I haven't needed it.
I don't know how to explain what this necklace means to me without sounding like I'm exaggerating.
But I'm not.
It's not just jewelry. It's the thing I hold onto when I can't hold onto anything else.
Some things are meant to last through everything.
Viole Grace Pearl Cross Necklace. Lifetime warranty. Built for real life.
I just saw they're doing 60% off. I don't know when it ends but that's the price I paid and I'd pay double knowing what I know now.
